title: Hash-routed coffee roaster site with a subscription price builder
prompt:
Build a small multi-page website for Ember & Oak, a small-batch coffee roaster that sells a bean subscription. It should feel warm, premium and hand-crafted. Deliver one index.html that uses hash routing with four routes: #/ (Home), #/beans, #/subscribe and #/faq.

Routing: the header nav (Home, Beans, Subscribe, FAQ) marks the current route with aria-current='page' and a visible active style. document.title is 'Ember & Oak · Small-batch coffee' on Home and '<Page> · Ember & Oak' elsewhere (for example 'Beans · Ember & Oak'). Only the current view is shown, the browser Back button returns to the previous route, opening index.html without a hash shows Home, and any unknown hash such as #/shop shows a 'Page not found' view with a 'Back to home' link.

Home: the headline 'Coffee worth waking up for', a 'Build your subscription' button that goes to #/subscribe, and three steps illustrated with inline SVG.

Beans: six coffee cards with name, origin, roast, tasting notes and price per 250g bag: Kiambu AA (Kenya, Light, $19), Huila Pink Bourbon (Colombia, Light, $21), Yirgacheffe Kochere (Ethiopia, Light, $18), Cerrado Natural (Brazil, Medium, $15), Antigua Pastoral (Guatemala, Medium, $16) and Sumatra Mandheling (Indonesia, Dark, $17). Add roast filter buttons All, Light, Medium and Dark, a sort select (Price: low to high, Price: high to low, Name A–Z) that combines with the filter, and a line such as 'Showing 3 of 6 coffees'.

Subscribe: a plan builder with bag size (250g or 1kg), bags per delivery (a stepper from 1 to 4 that cannot go outside that range) and frequency (Every week, Every 2 weeks, Every month); the default is 250g, 1 bag, Every month. Subscription bags are the roaster's choice at a flat price: $16 per 250g bag and $54 per 1kg bag. Weekly gets 10% off, every 2 weeks 5% off, monthly no discount. Shipping is $5.00 per delivery, or Free when the discounted per-delivery subtotal is $40.00 or more. A live summary shows Subtotal (before discount), Discount, Shipping, Per delivery (discounted subtotal plus shipping) and Per month (per delivery × 4, 2 or 1 deliveries), always in dollars with two decimals; the default shows $21.00 per delivery and $21.00 per month. Save the builder choices in localStorage and restore them after a reload.

FAQ: five questions in an accessible accordion: each question is a button with aria-expanded, and clicking one toggles only its own answer.

At 390px wide the nav collapses into a menu button that opens the four links, and the bean cards and the builder fit the screen.
interaction_hints: Routes: in one interact call use eval to set location.hash to '#/beans', '#/subscribe', '#/faq' and '#/shop' (wait 300 ms after each) and eval document.title plus document.querySelector('[aria-current=page]')?.textContent each time; then eval history.back() and check the previous view returns; also click the nav links themselves. Deep link: eval location.hash='#/faq', then reload and screenshot. Beans: click text=Light, then use select on the sort control (find its selector in the source) with 'Price: high to low', screenshot; then All with 'Price: low to high' and 'Name A–Z'. Subscribe: click the size, stepper and frequency controls to reach each rubric scenario and screenshot the summary; press minus at 1 bag and plus at 4 bags to check clamping. Persistence: in one call choose 1kg, 3 bags, Every 2 weeks, reload (re-open #/subscribe if needed), screenshot. FAQ: click two questions and eval their aria-expanded values. Mobile: run interact with --width 390 --height 844 and take full_page screenshots. Click the menu button there.

rubric.criterion: The nav has Home, Beans, Subscribe and FAQ; the current route's link has aria-current='page' and a visible active style, and document.title is exactly 'Ember & Oak · Small-batch coffee' on Home, 'Beans · Ember & Oak', 'Subscribe · Ember & Oak' and 'FAQ · Ember & Oak' on the other routes.

Routing works: nav clicks switch views and the hash without a full reload, only one view is visible at a time, history.back() returns to the previous view, and loading index.html#/faq directly shows the FAQ.
An unknown hash such as #/shop shows a 'Page not found' view whose 'Back to home' link returns to Home; index.html without a hash shows Home.
Home shows the headline 'Coffee worth waking up for', three SVG-illustrated steps, and a 'Build your subscription' button that navigates to #/subscribe.

Beans filter and sort combine: Light shows exactly Kiambu AA, Huila Pink Bourbon and Yirgacheffe Kochere with 'Showing 3 of 6 coffees', and with 'Price: high to low' they are ordered $21, $19, $18; All with 'Price: low to high' runs from Cerrado Natural $15 to Huila Pink Bourbon $21; 'Name A–Z' starts with Antigua Pastoral and ends with Yirgacheffe Kochere.

The builder math is exact: the default shows Per delivery $21.00 and Per month $21.00; 250g, 2 bags, Every 2 weeks shows Subtotal $32.00, Discount $1.60, Shipping $5.00, Per delivery $35.40, Per month $70.80; 1kg, 1 bag, Every week shows Discount $5.40, Shipping Free, Per delivery $48.60, Per month $194.40.
250g, 2 bags, Every week shows Per delivery $33.80 and Per month $135.20, and the bag stepper cannot go below 1 or above 4.
After choosing 1kg, 3 bags and Every 2 weeks and reloading, the builder restores those choices and shows Per delivery $153.90 and Per month $307.80.
The FAQ has five questions rendered as buttons whose aria-expanded flips between true and false; clicking one opens or closes only its own answer.
At 390px the nav is a menu button that reveals the four links, the bean cards stack in one column, and the builder controls and summary fit without clipping or overlap.
It looks like a premium roaster: a warm, consistent palette, a clear type hierarchy, even spacing between sections, and summary amounts aligned in a column.

title: Accessible illustrator portfolio with deep-linked keyboard lightbox
prompt:
Build a portfolio website for Mira Okafor, an independent illustrator who makes bold, colorful editorial and picture-book art. Playful but curated, like a gallery wall: a warm off-white background, one or two saturated accents and generous whitespace. There are no photos: every artwork is an original small illustration drawn with inline SVG, each clearly different from the others.

Work: exactly 12 artworks in this order, each tile labeled with its title and category: Paper Moon (Picture Books), The Night Market (Editorial), Fox in the Snow (Picture Books), Rising Rents (Editorial), Loop Coffee Co. (Brand), The Last Lighthouse (Picture Books), Election Night (Editorial), Seedling Studio (Brand), Deep Water (Editorial), Grandma's Garden (Picture Books), Pulse Running Club (Brand) and Heatwave (Editorial).

Filters: buttons 'All (12)', 'Editorial (5)', 'Picture Books (4)' and 'Brand (3)'; the active one has aria-pressed='true'. Filtering sets the URL hash to #/work, #/work/editorial, #/work/picture-books or #/work/brand, and loading the page with one of those hashes applies that filter.

Lightbox: every tile is a real button with aria-label 'Open <title>'. It opens a dialog (role='dialog', aria-modal='true', aria-labelledby pointing at the title) with a larger version of the same art, the title, the category, a one-line caption and a counter such as '2 / 5' that counts within the current filter. ArrowRight and ArrowLeft go to the next and previous artwork within the current filter and wrap around. Escape or the × button closes it and returns focus to the tile that opened it, and Tab only cycles through the dialog's controls while it is open. Opening an artwork sets the hash to #/art/<slug> (lowercase title, apostrophes and periods removed, spaces as hyphens, e.g. #/art/grandmas-garden, #/art/loop-coffee-co); closing restores the filter's hash; loading an #/art/ hash directly opens that artwork with the counter out of 12.

About: a short bio, an SVG self-portrait and a list of clients.

Contact: the heading 'Have a project in mind?', the email hello@miraokafor.art as a mailto link, and a form with name, email, message and Send. On submit show messages under the fields: 'Please enter your name', 'Please enter a valid email' and 'Message must be at least 20 characters'; set aria-invalid='true' on each invalid field and move focus to the first one. A valid submission replaces the form with 'Thanks, <name>! I will reply within two working days.'

Every interactive element shows a clearly visible focus ring when reached with the keyboard. At 390px the gallery shows one or two columns, the filter buttons wrap, and the lightbox fits the screen.
interaction_hints: Filters: click text=Editorial (5), screenshot, and eval location.hash plus [...document.querySelectorAll('[aria-pressed=true]')].map(e=>e.textContent). Lightbox, all in one call: click text=Editorial (5); click [aria-label='Open Rising Rents']; screenshot; eval location.hash; press ArrowRight 4 times with a screenshot after each; press ArrowLeft; press Tab 8 times then eval !!document.activeElement.closest('[role=dialog]'); press Escape; eval document.activeElement.getAttribute('aria-label') and location.hash. Under All, open Paper Moon and press ArrowLeft. Eval the dialog's role, aria-modal and the text of its aria-labelledby target. Deep links: eval location.hash='#/art/grandmas-garden', reload, screenshot; same with '#/work/brand'. Contact: click Send with empty fields, screenshot, eval the aria-invalid attributes and document.activeElement.name; then type name Ada, email ada@example.com and a 25-character message and submit. Focus rings: press Tab 5 times from the top and screenshot. Mobile: run interact with --width 390 --height 844 and take full_page screenshots. Open one artwork there too.

rubric.criterion: The gallery has the 12 titles in the requested order with their categories, each a distinct SVG illustration (not emoji, blank shapes or placeholder text), and the filters read 'All (12)', 'Editorial (5)', 'Picture Books (4)' and 'Brand (3)'.

Editorial shows exactly The Night Market, Rising Rents, Election Night, Deep Water and Heatwave and Brand shows exactly Loop Coffee Co., Seedling Studio and Pulse Running Club; only the active filter has aria-pressed='true'; the hash becomes #/work/editorial or #/work/brand; loading index.html#/work/brand shows the three brand pieces with Brand pressed.
Each tile is a button with aria-label 'Open <title>', and the lightbox has role='dialog', aria-modal='true' and aria-labelledby pointing at an element containing the artwork title.
With Editorial active, opening Rising Rents shows a larger version of the same artwork with its title, 'Editorial', a caption and the counter '2 / 5', and the hash becomes #/art/rising-rents.

ArrowRight from Rising Rents goes Election Night 3 / 5, Deep Water 4 / 5, Heatwave 5 / 5, then wraps to The Night Market 1 / 5, and ArrowLeft goes back to Heatwave 5 / 5; under All, ArrowLeft from Paper Moon shows Heatwave 12 / 12.

Escape and the × button both close the dialog; after Escape the focused element is the 'Open Rising Rents' tile and the hash is #/work/editorial again; while open, 8 Tab presses keep focus inside the dialog.
Loading index.html#/art/grandmas-garden opens Grandma's Garden directly with the counter '10 / 12'.

Submitting the empty form shows 'Please enter your name', 'Please enter a valid email' and 'Message must be at least 20 characters' under the fields, sets aria-invalid='true' on all three and focuses the name field; a valid submission for Ada shows 'Thanks, Ada! I will reply within two working days.'
Tabbing through the page shows a clearly visible focus ring on filter buttons, tiles and form controls (not the default hidden outline).
At 390px the gallery has one or two columns, the filter buttons wrap without overflow, and the open lightbox fits the screen with its art, text, counter and close button visible.
It reads as a curated illustrator portfolio: warm off-white ground, a restrained set of saturated accents, artworks in one consistent style, even grid gaps, and a clear heading hierarchy.

title: SaaS pricing page with currency, annual discount and seat math
prompt:
Create the pricing page for Lumetric, a B2B product-analytics platform. Dark navy theme with one electric accent color and crisp, high-contrast type.

Layout: a nav (SVG logo mark with the Lumetric wordmark, links Product, Pricing and Docs, and a 'Book a demo' button), the heading 'Pricing that scales with your team', the billing controls, three plan cards (Starter, Growth highlighted as 'Most popular', Enterprise), a Growth seat calculator, a feature comparison table, a four-question FAQ and a footer.

Billing controls: a Monthly / Annual switch labeled 'Save 20%' and a currency select with USD, EUR and GBP. Base monthly prices in USD: Starter 49 and Growth 199; Enterprise always shows 'Custom'. Rates: 1 USD = 0.92 EUR = 0.79 GBP. Price rule: start from the USD monthly price, take 20% off if Annual, convert, then round to the nearest whole unit. Show the symbol before the number with thousands separators ($, €, £) followed by '/mo'. Under each price show 'Billed monthly', or with Annual 'Billed annually: <symbol><rounded monthly × 12>' (for example Starter in USD with Annual: $39/mo, billed annually $468).

Seat calculator for Growth: Growth includes 5 seats and each extra seat adds 12 USD per month; the discount, conversion and rounding rules apply to the whole monthly total. A range slider (1–50) and a number input stay in sync, and typed values outside 1–50 clamp to the nearest limit. Show 'Includes 5 seats + <n> extra', the monthly total and the yearly total (rounded monthly × 12), updated live with the billing switch and currency.

Save the billing period, currency and seats in localStorage and restore them after a reload.

Comparison table: 12 feature rows in three groups (Analytics, Collaboration, Security) with a check, a dash or a short value per plan. Exactly 4 of the 12 rows are identical for all three plans. The header row stays visible (sticky) while you scroll through the table, and a 'Show differences only' toggle hides the 4 identical rows and shows them again when turned off.

On a 390px phone the plan cards stack, the calculator fits, and the comparison table scrolls inside its own container without widening the page.
interaction_hints: Pricing: screenshot the cards, click the Annual side of the switch, screenshot; select EUR and then GBP in the currency select (find its selector in the source) in both Monthly and Annual, screenshotting each. Calculator: set the range input with type (its selector, text '12'), switch to Annual and EUR, screenshot; type 60 and then 0 into the number input and press Tab after each to check clamping; set 3 seats in Monthly USD; set 50 seats in Monthly GBP. Persistence: in one call set Annual, GBP and 20 seats, reload, screenshot (expect £240 per month and £2,880 per year). Table: scroll through the table and screenshot to confirm the sticky header; click 'Show differences only' and eval the number of visible feature rows, then turn it off and count again. Mobile: run interact with --width 390 --height 844 and take full_page screenshots.

rubric.criterion: The nav, the heading 'Pricing that scales with your team', three plan cards with Growth marked 'Most popular', the calculator, the comparison table, a four-question FAQ and a footer are present in that order; Enterprise shows 'Custom' in every state.

In USD, Monthly shows Starter $49/mo and Growth $199/mo with 'Billed monthly'; Annual shows $39/mo and $159/mo with 'Billed annually: $468' and 'Billed annually: $1,908'; switching back restores the monthly values.
Currency conversion is exact: EUR Monthly €45 and €183, EUR Annual €36 and €146 (billed €432 and €1,752), GBP Monthly £39 and £157, GBP Annual £31 and £126 (billed £372 and £1,512).

The seat calculator is exact: 12 seats with Annual and EUR shows 'Includes 5 seats + 7 extra', €208 per month and €2,496 per year; 50 seats with Monthly and GBP shows £584 per month and £7,008 per year.
The slider and number input stay in sync; typing 60 becomes 50 and typing 0 becomes 1; 3 seats in Monthly USD shows 'Includes 5 seats + 0 extra' with $199 per month and $2,388 per year.
After choosing Annual, GBP and 20 seats and reloading, all three are restored and the calculator shows £240 per month and £2,880 per year, with the plan cards in GBP Annual (£31 and £126).
The comparison table has 12 feature rows under Analytics, Collaboration and Security; 'Show differences only' leaves exactly 8 rows and turning it off shows all 12 again.
The comparison table's header row with the plan names stays visible while scrolling through the table's rows.
The FAQ has four questions that expand and collapse individually when clicked.
At 390px the plan cards stack in one column, the calculator fits the screen, and the comparison table scrolls inside its own container with no page-level horizontal overflow.

A credible enterprise look: one dark navy palette with a single accent used sparingly, body text contrast of at least 4.5:1, prices set in aligned tabular figures, and consistent card spacing and radii.

title: Three-step donation flow with fee, match and card validation
prompt:
Design a donation page for Tidewater Project, a nonprofit that removes plastic from coastlines, for its campaign Clear the Current. Bright and hopeful: ocean blues, teal and a warm sand accent, with SVG wave dividers between sections.

Page: a header with an SVG logo and a 'Donate' link to the form; a hero with the headline 'Clear the Current' and an SVG ocean illustration; a campaign bar reading '$412,800 raised of $500,000' with the percentage to one decimal (82.6%) and a matching progress bar; a three-step donation form; a footer.

Step 1, Amount: buttons $25, $50, $100 and $250, a custom whole-dollar amount (5 to 10,000; otherwise show 'Enter an amount between $5 and $10,000' and block Next), a One-time / Monthly switch and a checkbox 'Cover the 3% processing fee'. Gifts are matched 1:1 by the Blue Current Fund up to $500 per donor, and every dollar of gift plus match (fee excluded) removes 2 lb of plastic. A live summary shows Gift, Fee (3% of the gift rounded to the cent, $0.00 when unchecked), Total today, 'Matched: +$<match>' and 'Removes <n> lb of plastic' with thousands separators (e.g. 3,500 lb).

Step 2, Details: first name ('Enter your first name'), last name ('Enter your last name'), email ('Enter a valid email address'), country (United States, Canada, United Kingdom) and postal code: the US needs exactly 5 digits ('ZIP code must be 5 digits'), Canada needs letter-digit-letter digit-letter-digit with an optional space ('Enter a postal code like K1A 0B1'), the UK just must not be empty ('Enter a postcode').

Step 3, Payment: card number (spaces allowed) with 16 digits that passes the Luhn check ('Card number is invalid'), expiry as MM/YY with a month from 01 to 12 ('Enter a valid expiry date'), and a CVC of exactly 3 digits ('CVC must be 3 digits'). The submit button reads 'Donate $<total>', or 'Donate $<total>/month' for monthly gifts.

Behavior: a step indicator (Amount, Details, Payment) marks the current step with aria-current='step'; Back and Next keep every value; errors appear under their fields, invalid fields get aria-invalid='true', and an aria-live region says 'Please fix <n> fields' with the exact count. On success show 'Thank you, <first name>!' with a receipt (gift, fee, total, one-time or monthly, matched amount), and the campaign bar adds the gift plus the match (a $250 gift gives $413,300 raised and 82.7%). All money shows two decimals except in the campaign bar.

At 390px everything stacks and the form fits the screen.
interaction_hints: Step 1: click text=$50 and screenshot the summary; click text=$100, check the fee checkbox, screenshot; type 1250 into the custom amount field (find its selector), screenshot; then 33, then 4 and 10001 and click Next after each invalid one. Step 2 (one call that first completes step 1): click Next with empty fields, screenshot, eval the aria-live region's text and the aria-invalid attributes; enter ZIP 1234 for the United States; select Canada and try 12345 then k1a0b1; select United Kingdom with an empty postcode. Step 3: try card 4242 4242 4242 4241, expiry 13/29 and CVC 12, then 4242 4242 4242 4242, 12/29, 123. Use Back from step 3 to step 1 and screenshot to confirm values are kept. Full success scenario in one call: $250 + fee, One-time, Ana Silva, ana@example.com, United States, 94105, the valid card; screenshot the receipt and the campaign bar. Repeat once with Monthly to read the button label. Eval document.querySelector('[aria-current=step]') textContent on each step. Mobile: run interact with --width 390 --height 844 and take full_page screenshots.

rubric.criterion: The page has the header with an SVG logo and a Donate link, the hero 'Clear the Current' with an SVG ocean illustration, wave dividers, the campaign bar '$412,800 raised of $500,000' showing 82.6% with a bar about 83% full, the form and a footer.

With $50 and no fee the summary shows Gift $50.00, Fee $0.00, Total today $50.00, 'Matched: +$50.00' and 'Removes 200 lb of plastic'; with $100 and the fee checked it shows Fee $3.00, Total today $103.00, 'Matched: +$100.00' and 'Removes 400 lb of plastic'.

Custom 1250 with the fee shows Fee $37.50, Total today $1,287.50, 'Matched: +$500.00' and 'Removes 3,500 lb of plastic'; custom 33 with the fee shows Fee $0.99, Total today $33.99 and 132 lb; 4 and 10001 show 'Enter an amount between $5 and $10,000' and Next does not advance.
Choosing Monthly makes the step 3 button read 'Donate $<total>/month' (e.g. 'Donate $257.50/month' for $250 with the fee) and the receipt says monthly.

Step 2 validation is exact: Next with every field empty shows 'Enter your first name', 'Enter your last name', 'Enter a valid email address' and 'ZIP code must be 5 digits' and the live region says 'Please fix 4 fields'; US 1234 is rejected; Canada rejects 12345 with 'Enter a postal code like K1A 0B1' but accepts k1a0b1; the UK with an empty postcode shows 'Enter a postcode'.
Invalid fields carry aria-invalid='true' (removed once fixed), and aria-current='step' moves from Amount to Details to Payment as the user advances.
Step 3 rejects 4242 4242 4242 4241 with 'Card number is invalid', 13/29 with 'Enter a valid expiry date' and CVC 12 with 'CVC must be 3 digits', and accepts 4242 4242 4242 4242, 12/29 and 123.
Back and Next keep every value: returning from step 3 to step 1 still shows the chosen amount, frequency and fee checkbox, and step 2 still holds the typed details.

A $250 one-time gift with the fee from Ana shows 'Thank you, Ana!' with Gift $250.00, Fee $7.50, Total $257.50, One-time and Matched $250.00, and the campaign bar updates to $413,300 raised and 82.7%.
At 390px the hero, campaign bar and all three form steps fit the screen in one column with full-width amount buttons and no clipped or overlapping text.

Bright and hopeful in a consistent way: ocean blues and teal with a sand accent, smooth SVG wave dividers, a clear hierarchy in the form, and error text that is readable and clearly tied to its field.

title: Conference site with time-zone schedule and conflict-aware agenda
prompt:
Build the website for Edgecase 2026, a frontend engineering conference in Lisbon on 14–16 October 2026. Bold and energetic: oversized type, a black and off-white base with electric lime and violet accents, and visible grid lines.

Sections: a sticky nav (logo, Speakers, Schedule, Venue, Tickets and a 'My agenda (N)' link to #/agenda); a hero with the headline 'Build for the edge cases', 14–16 October 2026 and Lisbon; Speakers (8 cards with CSS or SVG avatars); Schedule; Venue (Lisbon Tech Hub, an address and an SVG map); Tickets (Early Bird €299 marked Sold out with a disabled button, Standard €449, Team (5+) €399 per person); footer.

Schedule (Lisbon local time, start–end, title, speaker, track):
Day 1 · Wed 14 Oct: 09:00–12:00 Building a design token pipeline (Ana Ferreira, Design Systems); 09:00–12:00 Profiling React in production (Tom Becker, Performance); 13:30–16:30 Accessible forms from scratch (Priya Nair, Accessibility); 13:30–16:30 Edge rendering deep dive (Kenji Mori, Performance); 18:00–20:00 Welcome drinks (Community).
Day 2 · Thu 15 Oct: 09:30–10:15 Keynote: The web at the edge (Marta Silva, Performance); 10:15–11:00 Container queries in the wild (Sam Okoro, Design Systems); 10:30–11:00 Screen readers are users too (Hana Kim, Accessibility); 11:15–12:00 Shipping less JavaScript (Diego Ramos, Performance); 14:00–14:45 Tokens across ten brands (Ana Ferreira, Design Systems); 18:30–19:15 Lightning talks (Community).
Day 3 · Fri 16 Oct: 07:30–08:15 Morning run along the Tagus (Community); 09:30–10:15 Motion without nausea (Hana Kim, Accessibility); 10:30–11:15 INP in the real world (Tom Becker, Performance); 11:30–12:15 Design systems at scale (Lucas Meyer, Design Systems); 16:00–16:45 Closing keynote: Edge cases are the main case (Priya Nair, Accessibility); 20:00–23:00 Closing party (Community).

Schedule UI: day tabs following the WAI-ARIA tabs pattern (role='tab', aria-selected, ArrowLeft/ArrowRight move between tabs), track chips (All, Performance, Design Systems, Accessibility, Community) that combine with the day, and a labeled time-zone select: Lisbon (default), UTC, New York, San Francisco, Tokyo. Use these fixed offsets for the conference dates, not the visitor's zone: Lisbon UTC+1, UTC+0, New York UTC−4, San Francisco UTC−7, Tokyo UTC+9. Show start–end in 24-hour HH:MM in the chosen zone, and when a converted start falls on a different calendar day than the session's Lisbon date, add '+1 day' or '−1 day' next to the time. Sessions stay under their Lisbon day tab.

Agenda: every session has a star button (aria-pressed, aria-label 'Add <title> to my agenda') and the nav count updates. #/agenda lists the starred sessions in chronological order, grouped by Lisbon day, in the chosen time zone; with nothing starred it says 'Your agenda is empty'. Two starred sessions conflict when their times overlap (an end time equal to a start time is not a conflict); both are marked 'Conflicts with <other title>'. Starred sessions and the time zone persist in localStorage.

At 390px the schedule stacks, the tabs and chips wrap or scroll, and nothing overflows the page.
interaction_hints: Schedule: click each day tab and screenshot; focus a tab and press ArrowRight/ArrowLeft, eval document.activeElement.textContent and aria-selected. Day 2 + chip Accessibility, screenshot. Time zones: use select on the time-zone control (find its selector) with New York, UTC, Tokyo and San Francisco, screenshotting Day 2 and Day 3 each time. Agenda in one call: star (via [aria-label='Add <title> to my agenda']) Closing keynote, Morning run along the Tagus, Keynote: The web at the edge and Profiling React in production in that order, eval location.hash='#/agenda', screenshot; then star Container queries in the wild and Screen readers are users too, screenshot the agenda, unstar Screen readers and screenshot. Persistence: in one call star two sessions, pick San Francisco, reload, screenshot the nav count and #/agenda. Also open #/agenda on a fresh page for the empty state. Mobile: run interact with --width 390 --height 844 and take full_page screenshots.

rubric.criterion: The sticky nav shows Speakers, Schedule, Venue, Tickets and 'My agenda (0)'; the hero shows 'Build for the edge cases', 14–16 October 2026 and Lisbon; there are 8 speaker cards with drawn avatars, a Lisbon Tech Hub venue with an SVG map, and tickets Early Bird €299 (Sold out, disabled), Standard €449 and Team (5+) €399 per person.
In Lisbon time the three tabs list exactly the given sessions with their start–end times, speakers and color-coded track tags.

Only the selected day's sessions are visible, the selected tab has aria-selected='true', ArrowRight/ArrowLeft move between tabs, and Day 2 with the Accessibility chip shows only 'Screen readers are users too'.

Time-zone conversion is exact: New York shows the Day 2 keynote at 04:30–05:15, UTC shows it at 08:30–09:15, Tokyo shows Lightning talks at 02:30–03:15 and Closing party at 04:00–07:00 both with '+1 day', and San Francisco shows Morning run along the Tagus at 23:30–00:15 with '−1 day'.

Star buttons toggle aria-pressed and update 'My agenda (N)'; after starring Closing keynote, Morning run, the Day 2 keynote and Profiling React in that order, #/agenda lists Profiling React (Wed 14), the Day 2 keynote (Thu 15), Morning run and Closing keynote (Fri 16) in that order.

Conflicts are exact: the Day 2 keynote plus Container queries in the wild show no conflict; adding Screen readers are users too marks Container queries and Screen readers with 'Conflicts with' naming each other while the keynote stays unflagged; unstarring Screen readers clears the marks.
After a reload the starred sessions, the nav count and the chosen time zone are restored, and #/agenda in San Francisco shows Morning run along the Tagus at 23:30 with '−1 day'.
Loading index.html#/agenda with nothing starred shows 'Your agenda is empty'.
Star buttons carry aria-label 'Add <title> to my agenda', and the time-zone select has an associated visible label.
At 390px sessions stack in one column with times, titles and tags readable, the tabs and chips wrap or scroll inside the screen, and nothing overflows the page.
Bold and consistent: oversized headline type, black and off-white base with lime and violet used consistently for tracks and states, visible grid lines, and tight, even spacing.

title: Bilingual restaurant site with combined menu filters and rule-based booking
prompt:
Make a website for Osteria Lume, a small neighborhood Italian restaurant known for handmade pasta and a wood-fired oven. Elegant and intimate: deep olive green and cream, a serif for headings (DejaVu Serif or Liberation Serif) with a clean sans for body text, and thin decorative dividers.

Sections: header (wordmark 'Osteria Lume', links Menu, About, Visit, Reserve and an EN / IT language switch), hero ('Handmade pasta, wood-fired evenings' with a 'Reserve a table' button and a CSS or SVG illustration), Menu, About, Visit (address, opening hours for all seven days with Monday closed, phone), Reserve, footer.
